target: fatal accidents involving Boeing commercial jets

evidence.scope: global commercial aviation under IATA methodology
evidence.observation: IATA reports ten fatal accidents in 2016: five jet and five turboprop. The five fatal jet accidents are West Air Sweden CRJ200, FlyDubai B737-800, EgyptAir A320, LaMia RJ85 and Aerosucre B727. IATA's then-current fatal-accident metric counted onboard fatalities only, so Emirates EK521 is not captured by that five-event fatal-jet count.
evidence.use: annual-universe and target-membership reconciliation with explicit onboard-only limitation

evidence.publisher: Flight Safety Foundation summarizing IATA Safety Report 2016
evidence.source_title: IATA Measures Improvement in Commercial Aviation Safety
evidence.observation: FSF confirms 268 onboard fatalities and that IATA's report excluded people killed on the ground from the fatality count; EgyptAir 804 and LaMia 2933 are explicitly included in the 2016 accident statistics.
Investigation finished; commercial air transport; FlyDubai Boeing 737-800 A6-FDN, serial 40241; 62 fatalities.

evidence.publisher: UAE GCAA Air Accident Investigation Sector
evidence.observation: Emirates scheduled passenger flight UAE521, Boeing 777-31H A6-EMW, serial 32700; all occupants survived but one firefighter was fatally injured; occurrence classified as an Annex 13 accident.
Boeing 727-2JO HK4544, serial 21105, Aerosucre, non-scheduled cargo air transport; five fatalities among six occupants.

evidence.publisher: The Boeing Company / 2016 commercial-jet statistical reconciliation
evidence.scope: worldwide commercial-jet accidents under Boeing definitions
evidence.observation: The annual Boeing reconciliation is consistent with FlyDubai, LaMia and Aerosucre contributing 138 onboard fatalities and Emirates contributing one external fatality; non-Boeing fatal jet cases remain outside the target.
evidence.use: independent manufacturer reconciliation and external-fatality control
